results.snippet: Post-maintenance surveillance failure HPCI Train A. Coupling slippage under load confirmed by disassembly inspection — coupling bore damaged due to insufficient torque preload. Same part type from lot VEN-2026-Q1-HC7 installed on Train B during same outage window. Vendor advisory VA-2025-HC7-001 received November 2025 identifies this lot's sensitivity to torque specification deviation. Advisory was not dispositioned into work order or procedure change. This represents a common-cause failure coupling mechanism: same lot, same crew, same procedure gap, simultaneous failure. CCF evaluation required per plant CCF procedures.

Vendor Service Advisory — HydroCoup coupling lot HC7: Torque sensitivity. Insufficient torque preload during installation may cause coupling slip under high-load conditions. Required torque specification: 485 ft-lbs minimum. Standard station procedure may specify 450 ft-lbs for similar-size couplings — the HC7 lot requires 8% higher torque due to modified bore geometry. Installations performed with insufficient torque will not be detectable during no-load rotation test but will fail under full pump load. All installations from lot HC7 should be verified or re-torqued to 485 ft-lbs minimum.

HPCI injection flow acceptance criterion: minimum 5000 gpm within 25 seconds of pump start during surveillance test conditions. Failure to meet this criterion constitutes an operability concern and requires immediate condition report per 10CFR50.73 reportability evaluation. Note: The surveillance procedure does not include vendor coupling torque acceptance criteria. Coupling-specific torque verification requirements are contained only in vendor technical manual appendix references, which are not translated into station procedures.
